questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Although he was tired, / but he completed / the audit report.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'but he completed'. 'Although' and 'but' should not be used together; drop 'but'.

questions.q: The audit was conducted ____ the supervision of the regional office.
questions.x: 'Under the supervision of' is the idiomatic phrase.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'Fear of heights'
questions.x: 'Acrophobia' means fear of heights.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'A white elephant'
o: A possession that costs more to maintain than it is worth
questions.x: 'A white elephant' means: a possession that costs more to maintain than it is worth.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Imminent'.
questions.x: 'Imminent' means impending. 'Remote' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The officer as well as / his staff members / were praised for the work.
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'were praised for the work'. With 'as well as', the verb agrees with the first subject 'officer': 'was praised'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A person who cannot be corrected'
questions.x: 'Incorrigible' means a person who cannot be corrected.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: RESILIENT
questions.x: 'Resilient' means tough. 'Fragile' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To add fuel to the fire'
o: To make a bad situation worse
questions.x: 'To add fuel to the fire' means: to make a bad situation worse.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: RELUCTANT
questions.x: 'Reluctant' is the opposite of 'Eager'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Reluctant'.

questions.q: What is described as the next challenge for renewable energy?
questions.x: Answer: 'Storage and grid management'. The second sentence identifies storage and grid management. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Renewable energy has become cheaper than many expected, but the sun does not shine at night and the wind does not blow on demand. The next challenge is storage and grid management. Batteries, pumped hydro and smarter grids that shift demand to sunny hours can make clean power reliable. The transition will depend as much on engineering of the grid as on the number of solar panels installed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way to make clean power reliable?
questions.x: Answer: 'Building new coal plants'. Coal plants are not mentioned. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Renewable energy has become cheaper than many expected, but the sun does not shine at night and the wind does not blow on demand. The next challenge is storage and grid management. Batteries, pumped hydro and smarter grids that shift demand to sunny hours can make clean power reliable. The transition will depend as much on engineering of the grid as on the number of solar panels installed.

questions.q: The title 'Lokmanya' was associated with:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Valentine Chirol called him the 'father of Indian unrest'.

questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn after violence at:
questions.x: A mob burnt a police station at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur) in February 1922.

questions.q:
Match the centre of the Revolt of 1857 with its leader:
Centre:
A. Kanpur
B. Jhansi
C. Lucknow
D. Arrah (Bihar)
Leader:
1. Begum Hazrat Mahal
2. Kunwar Singh
3. Nana Saheb
4. Rani Lakshmibai
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Kanpur) → 3 (Nana Saheb); B (Jhansi) → 4 (Rani Lakshmibai); C (Lucknow) → 1 (Begum Hazrat Mahal); D (Arrah (Bihar)) → 2 (Kunwar Singh).
Other leaders: Bahadur Shah Zafar (Delhi, nominal), Khan Bahadur Khan (Bareilly), Maulvi Ahmadullah (Faizabad).

questions.q: The Faraizi movement in Bengal was founded by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Haji Shariatullah. His son Dudu Miyan led it against zamindars.

questions.q: The 'Bijolia movement' in Rajasthan was a:
o: Peasant movement against excessive taxes by the jagirdar
questions.x: Correct answer: Peasant movement against excessive taxes by the jagirdar. It was led by Vijay Singh Pathik among others.

questions.q: The Ryotwari system, under which revenue was settled directly with cultivators, was associated mainly with:
o: Holt Mackenzie in the North-West Provinces
questions.x: Correct answer: Thomas Munro in Madras. The Mahalwari system was associated with Holt Mackenzie.

questions.q: The integration of princely states after independence was led by:
o: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel with V. P. Menon
questions.x: Most states acceded through the Instrument of Accession; Hyderabad, Junagadh and Kashmir were special cases.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Partition of Bengal was annulled at the Delhi Durbar.
questions.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled at the Delhi Durbar in 1911. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Who founded the Banaras Hindu University in 1916?
questions.x: Correct answer: Madan Mohan Malaviya. Annie Besant's Central Hindu College became its nucleus.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Annie Besant was the first woman president of the Congress.
2. Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman president of the Congress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Besant (1917) and Naidu (1925).

questions.q: The 'Startup Mahakumbh' and 'National Startup Day' are linked to which national initiative?
questions.x: Correct answer: Startup India. National Startup Day is 16 January.

questions.q: The 'India Semiconductor Mission' was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: December 2021. It supports fabs, display fabs and ATMP/OSAT units.

questions.q: The headquarters of the World Intellectual Property Organization is located in:
questions.x: World Intellectual Property Organization: headquartered in Geneva.

questions.q: INS Vikrant, commissioned in September 2022, is:
o: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier
questions.x: Correct answer: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier. It was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited.

questions.q: The 2025 International Booker Prize was won by 'Heart Lamp', a collection of short stories by:
questions.x: It was the first Kannada work to win; translated by Deepa Bhasthi. Geetanjali Shree won in 2022 for 'Tomb of Sand'.

questions.q: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was enacted in:
questions.x: It establishes the Data Protection Board of India; its rules were notified in 2025.

questions.q: The 17th BRICS Summit (July 2025) was hosted by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Brazil (Rio de Janeiro). India holds the BRICS chairship in 2026.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 15 September?
questions.x: 15 September is Engineers' Day (M. Visvesvaraya).

questions.q: 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign is associated with:
o: Celebrating Independence Day by hoisting the national flag at homes
questions.x: Correct answer: Celebrating Independence Day by hoisting the national flag at homes. It began in 2022 as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav.

questions.q: 'POSHAN Abhiyaan', launched in 2018, primarily aims to reduce:
o: Stunting, under-nutrition, anaemia and low birth weight
questions.x: Correct answer: Stunting, under-nutrition, anaemia and low birth weight. It is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

questions.q: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble are borrowed from:
questions.x: The French motto of 'Liberté, égalité, fraternité' inspired these ideals.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vice-President of India:
1. The Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. State legislators also vote in the election of the Vice-President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Only MPs (elected and nominated) vote; State legislators do not.

questions.q: Article 301 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court (advisory jurisdiction)
Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse
Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States
questions.x: Article 301: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.

questions.q: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the selection committee consists of:
o: The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM
The PM, the CJI and the Leader of Opposition
The Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.x: The 2023 Act replaced the CJI (as directed interimly in Anoop Baranwal, 2023) with a Cabinet Minister.

questions.q: The constitutional amendment that gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes was enacted in the year:
questions.x: This was the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018.

questions.q: The new criminal laws that replaced the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act came into force on:
questions.x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force on 1 July 2024.

questions.q: The Delimitation Commission in India is constituted by:
o: The Central Government under a Delimitation Act passed by Parliament
questions.x: Correct answer: The Central Government under a Delimitation Act passed by Parliament. Its orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in court.

questions.q: A 'pocket veto' by the President refers to:
o: Keeping a bill pending indefinitely without assent or return
Returning a bill once for reconsideration
questions.x: The Constitution prescribes no time limit for presidential assent on ordinary bills (except money bills cannot be returned).

questions.q: Article 50 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Power of the President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
Protection of monuments and places of national importance
Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution
questions.x: Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive.

questions.q: Which writ is issued to a public official to perform a public duty that he has refused or failed to perform?
questions.x: Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or Governors, or private individuals.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): Revenue receipts 24,000; Non-debt capital receipts 1,000; Revenue expenditure 54,000 (of which interest payments 16,000); Capital expenditure 13,000. The primary deficit is:
questions.x:
Total expenditure = 54,000 + 13,000 = 67,000.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts) = 67,000 − 25,000 = 42,000.
Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest = 26,000.
Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts = 30,000.
Answer (primary): ₹26,000 crore.

questions.q: The 'Gift City' in Gujarat hosts India's first:
questions.x: Correct answer: International Financial Services Centre. IFSCA regulates financial services there.

questions.q: The C. Rangarajan Expert Group (2014) is associated with:
o: Comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households
questions.x: C. Rangarajan Expert Group (2014): Review of poverty measurement.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Commercial banks
2. Regional Rural Banks
3. Cooperative banks
4. Payment banks
How many of the above are regulated by the RBI?
questions.x:
4 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All four are regulated by the RBI (cooperative banks jointly with RCS/NABARD supervision for rural cooperatives).

questions.q: SEBI was given statutory powers — in which year?
questions.x: SEBI was given statutory powers in 1992.

questions.q: The 'Economic Survey' of India is prepared by:
o: The Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser
questions.x: Correct answer: The Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser. It is presented a day before the Budget.

questions.q: 'Make in India' was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: September 2014. It aimed to make India a global manufacturing hub.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.x: Correct answer: Corporation tax. The burden of a direct tax cannot be shifted.

questions.q: National Income in India is conventionally:
questions.x: NNP at factor cost (now basic prices framework) is called national income.

questions.q: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF), introduced in 2022, allows the RBI to:
o: Absorb liquidity from banks without giving collateral
questions.x: SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the liquidity adjustment facility corridor.

questions.q: Goodwill is classified as:
questions.x: Goodwill is an intangible asset; fictitious assets (like preliminary expenses written off over years earlier) have no realisable value.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹20,000, Debtors ₹45,000, Inventory ₹75,000, Prepaid expenses ₹2,500, Creditors ₹30,000, Bills payable ₹12,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹7,500. Its current ratio is:
The profits of a firm for the last 4 years were ₹38,000, ₹49,000, ₹61,000, ₹27,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 3 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹40,000; Purchases ₹2,70,000; Purchase returns ₹2,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹3,23,500; Closing stock ₹45,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 40,000 + 2,70,000 − 2,000 + 3,000 − 45,000 = ₹2,66,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 3,23,500 − 2,66,000 = ₹57,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Equity shareholders of a company are its:
questions.x: Correct answer: Owners. They bear residual risk and have voting rights.

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹1,60,000 and at the end ₹2,17,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹5,000 and withdrew ₹7,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 2,17,500 + 7,500 − 5,000 − 1,60,000 = ₹60,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: A product sells at ₹70 with a variable cost of ₹35 per unit. Fixed costs are ₹1,29,500. The break-even sales (in ₹) are:
questions.x:
P/V ratio = Contribution/Sales = 35/70 = 50%.
BEP sales = Fixed cost / P/V ratio = 1,29,500 / 0.5 = ₹2,59,000.

questions.q: An entry that affects both cash and bank columns of a cash book is called a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Contra entry. Contra entries are marked 'C' in the folio column.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹2,20,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 2,20,000 × (0.75)^3 = ₹92,812.50.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹55,000.)

questions.q: Recording assets at the price paid to acquire them rather than at market value follows the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Historical cost concept. Cost is objective and verifiable.

questions.q: Purchase of machinery is shown in the cash flow statement under:
questions.x: Acquisition and disposal of long-term assets are investing activities.

questions.q: When a bill receivable is discounted with the bank, the discount charged is debited to:
questions.x: Bank A/c Dr. (net), Discount A/c Dr. To Bills Receivable A/c.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹5,000 at the end of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 5,000 = ₹60,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the end of each month = 5.5 months.
Interest = 60,000 × 8% × 5.5/12 = ₹2,200.

questions.q: Contribution in marginal costing equals:
o: Fixed cost plus profit minus sales
questions.x: Correct answer: Sales minus variable cost. Contribution = Fixed cost + Profit.

questions.q: Worker Population Ratio (WPR) is defined as:
o: Employed persons as a percentage of the total population
Labour force as a percentage of the population
Unemployed as a percentage of the labour force
Workers in industry as a percentage of all workers
questions.x: Correct answer: Employed persons as a percentage of the total population. WPR measures the share of the population that is employed.

questions.q: The Seventh Central Pay Commission was chaired by:
questions.x: The 7th CPC (report 2015) recommended a minimum pay of ₹18,000 per month and a fitment factor of 2.57.

questions.q: Under Part A of the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, a first-time employee registered with EPFO receives:
o: One month's EPF wage up to ₹15,000, paid in two instalments
questions.x: First-time employees get one month's EPF wage capped at ₹15,000, in two instalments; part is kept in a savings instrument to encourage saving.

questions.q: The IR Code permits an individual worker to approach the Industrial Tribunal directly in disputes relating to discharge, dismissal or retrenchment:
o: Only after the appropriate government refers the dispute
After 45 days of applying to the conciliation officer
Only after the trade union espouses the cause
questions.x: Section 53 allows an individual worker to apply directly to the Tribunal after forty-five days from the application for conciliation.

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, a premises using power becomes a 'factory' when it employs at least:
questions.x: The threshold was raised from 10 to 20 workers with power and from 20 to 40 workers without power.

questions.q: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 granted registered unions which important protection?
o: Immunity from civil suits and criminal conspiracy for legitimate trade disputes
Exemption from income tax for members
questions.x: Sections 17 and 18 gave immunity against criminal conspiracy and civil suits for acts in furtherance of a trade dispute.

questions.q: The Union Budget 2025–26 announced which measure for gig and platform workers?
o: Identity cards, registration on e-Shram and health coverage under PM Jan Arogya Yojana
questions.x: The Budget proposed registration of about one crore gig workers on e-Shram with ID cards and healthcare under PM-JAY.

questions.q: Under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, which body is constituted at the district level to help rehabilitate freed bonded labourers?
questions.x: Vigilance Committees at the district and sub-divisional levels identify, release and rehabilitate bonded labourers.

questions.q: Which of the following is permitted for women workers under the OSH Code?
o: Work in mines, including below ground, subject to safeguards
Only day shifts in all establishments
No employment in mines at all
questions.x: The OSH Code allows women to work in all establishments, including underground mines during the day and in technical/supervisory roles at night, subject to safeguards.

questions.q: 'Productivity bargaining' links wage increases to:
o: Agreed changes in work practices that raise productivity
questions.x: Workers accept changes improving efficiency in exchange for higher pay.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 (now in the OSH Code):
1. It required employers to provide housing and medical facilities to resident workers.
2. It applied to tea, coffee, rubber and cinchona plantations.
3. It prohibited the employment of women in plantations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Act required housing, medical care, canteens, creches and education facilities for plantation workers. It did not bar women, who form a large part of the plantation workforce.

questions.q: A monthly-rated employee in a firm is paid salary for October on 12 November. Under the Code on Wages, this is:
o: Permissible for establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees
A violation, as monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month
Permissible, as wages may be paid by the 15th
Permissible if the employee agreed orally
questions.x: The Code requires monthly wages to be paid before the end of the 7th day of the succeeding month.

questions.q: What is the time limit for filing a claim for unpaid wages, bonus or less-than-minimum wages before the authority under the Code on Wages?
questions.x: Section 45 allows claims to be filed within three years from the date the claim arises.

questions.q: How many of the ILO's fundamental conventions has India ratified (as of 2025)?
questions.x: India has ratified C29, C105, C100, C111, C138 and C182; it has not ratified C87, C98, C155 and C187.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a 'collective agreement' outcome in Indian banking?
o: Bipartite settlement between IBA and bank unions on wage revision
questions.x: Bank wages are revised through bipartite settlements between the Indian Banks' Association and employee unions.

questions.q: 'Tripartism' in labour policy means decision-making through consultation among:
questions.x: Tripartism underlies the ILO and India's Indian Labour Conference and advisory boards under the Codes.

questions.q: An employee with monthly wages of ₹12,000 is covered under both EPF and ESI. Total statutory deduction from wages for these two schemes is:
questions.x: Correct answer: ₹1,530 (EPF ₹1,440 + ESI ₹90). Employee EPF 12% = ₹1,440; employee ESI 0.75% = ₹90; total ₹1,530.

questions.q: EPFO can recover arrears from a defaulting employer by modes similar to those under the Income Tax Act, such as:
o: Attachment and sale of property and arrest of the employer
questions.x: Sections 8B to 8G provide recovery through attachment, sale, appointment of receiver and arrest/detention.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹8,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹8,000 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 12%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 8,000) = ₹8,000.
Salary for computation = min(8,500, 8,000) = ₹8,000.
Annual bonus = 8,000 × 12 × 12% = ₹11,520. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: Under EPS 1995, a member who defers pension beyond 58 up to 60 gets an increase in pension of:
questions.x: The 2016 amendment allows deferment up to 60 with a 4% enhancement per year.

questions.q: The idea of a 'Universal Basic Income' was discussed in a full chapter of which Indian document?
questions.x: The Economic Survey 2016–17 discussed UBI as an alternative to multiple welfare schemes.

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, the term 'unorganised worker' covers:
o: Home-based, self-employed or wage workers in the unorganised sector, and workers in the organised sector not covered by specified Acts
questions.x: The broad definition enables registration on a national database and targeted schemes.

questions.q:
Match the NSAP component with its beneficiaries:
Component:
A. IGNOAPS
B. IGNWPS
C. IGNDPS
D. NFBS
Beneficiaries:
1. BPL persons aged 60 and above
2. BPL household on death of primary breadwinner
3. BPL widows aged 40–79
4. BPL persons with severe disability aged 18–79
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (IGNOAPS) → 1 (BPL persons aged 60 and above); B (IGNWPS) → 3 (BPL widows aged 40–79); C (IGNDPS) → 4 (BPL persons with severe disability aged 18–79); D (NFBS) → 2 (BPL household on death of primary breadwinner).
These are the main components; Annapurna provides foodgrains to eligible elderly not covered by IGNOAPS.

questions.q: The gratuity ceiling for Central Government employees was raised to ₹25 lakh from January 2024 when:
o: The Code on Social Security came into force
questions.x: As per the 7th CPC formula, the ceiling rises by 25% when DA reaches 50%; it became ₹25 lakh from 1 January 2024.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹9,500 and pensionable service of 27 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (9,500 × 27) / 70 = ₹3,664.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q: 'Social security' as defined by the ILO broadly means protection that society provides to its members through public measures against:
o: Economic and social distress caused by loss or reduction of earnings due to contingencies
questions.x: Contingencies include sickness, maternity, employment injury, unemployment, invalidity, old age and death.

questions.q: ESI benefits are broadly classified into medical benefit and cash benefits. Which of the following is a cash benefit?
questions.x: Cash benefits include sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants', unemployment allowance and funeral expenses.

questions.q: Interest payable by an employer for delayed remittance of EPF dues under Section 7Q is:
questions.x: Section 7Q prescribes simple interest at 12% per annum (or as specified) from the due date.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure altitude?
questions.x: Altimeter measures altitude.

questions.q: 'Antimicrobial resistance' arises mainly due to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Completing prescribed courses and avoiding self-medication help.

questions.q: In a computer, the 'motherboard' is:
o: The main circuit board connecting the CPU, memory and other components
questions.x: Correct answer: The main circuit board connecting the CPU, memory and other components. It houses slots and connectors for all major components.

questions.q: Why does a spoon in hot tea become hot?
o: Conduction of heat through the metal
questions.x: Correct answer: Conduction of heat through the metal. Metals are good conductors.

questions.q: 'Augmented reality' differs from 'virtual reality' in that AR:
o: Overlays digital information on the real world
questions.x: Correct answer: Overlays digital information on the real world. VR immerses users in a fully virtual environment.

questions.q: In computing, 'VPN' stands for:
questions.x: VPN = Virtual Private Network.

questions.q: Pasteurisation and rabies vaccine is credited to:
questions.x: Pasteurisation and rabies vaccine: Louis Pasteur.

questions.q: Insulin is secreted by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Pancreas (islets of Langerhans). Lack of insulin or resistance to it causes diabetes mellitus.

questions.q: Excess nutrients in water bodies leading to algal blooms is called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Eutrophication. It depletes dissolved oxygen and harms aquatic life.

questions.q: 'Bandwidth' in networking refers to:
o: The maximum data transfer rate of a connection
questions.x: Correct answer: The maximum data transfer rate of a connection. It is measured in bits per second (bps, Mbps, Gbps).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Keyboard
2. Scanner
3. Plotter
4. Microphone
How many of the above are input devices?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Keyboard, scanner and microphone are input devices; a plotter is an output device.

questions.q: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.x: Violet has the shortest wavelength; red is used for danger signals as it scatters least.

questions.q: Meena starts from point O and walks 17 km towards South, then turns left and walks 6 km, then turns left and walks 29 km, and finally turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -17 +29 = 12 km → 12 km North.
East–West: +6 -15 = -9 km → 9 km West.
Distance = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km, towards North-West.

questions.q: A train 130 m long running at 72 km/h crosses a platform in 26 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Distance covered in 26 s = 520 m = train + platform.
Platform = 520 − 130 = 390 m.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 50% above the cost price and allows a discount of 20% on the marked price. His gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 150.
SP after 20% discount = 150 × 0.8 = 120.
Gain = 120 − 100 = 20 on 100 → 20% gain.
Shortcut: m − d − md/100 = 50 − 20 − 10 = 20%.

questions.q: Team X and Team Y together can audit a ledger in 26 days. Team X alone can do it in 39 days. How many days will Team Y alone take?
questions.x:
Team Y's one-day work = 1/26 − 1/39 = (39 − 26)/1014 = 1/78.
So Team Y alone takes 78 days.

questions.q: There are 62 names in a queue at a counter. Sonal's name is 27th from the top. What is its position from the bottom?
questions.x: Position from bottom = Total − position from top + 1 = 62 − 27 + 1 = 36.

questions.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'PARTNER' be arranged so that all the vowels always come together?
questions.x:
Vowels: A, E; consonants: P, R, T, N, R.
Treat the vowels as one block → 6 units → 360 arrangements (R appears 2 times).
Vowels inside the block: 2 ways (all letters are distinct).
Total = 360 × 2 = 720.

questions.q: In a certain code language, BUDGET is written as FQHCIP. How is UNION written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare BUDGET → FQHCIP: B→F, U→Q, D→H…
Rule: letters in odd positions move 4 forward and letters in even positions move 4 backward.
Applying it to UNION gives YJMKR.

questions.q: ₹53,200 is divided among three branches in the ratio 5 : 7 : 2. The largest share is:
questions.x:
Sum of ratio terms = 5 + 7 + 2 = 14.
One part = 53,200 / 14 = ₹3,800.
Largest share = 7 × 3,800 = ₹26,600.

questions.q: A sum of money lent at simple interest amounts to ₹15,400 in 2 years and to ₹16,800 in 4 years. The rate of interest per annum is:

New establishments registered — 2018: 130  |  2019: 135  |  2020: 160  |  2021: 185  |  2022: 190.
What is the percentage change from 2020 to 2022?
questions.x:
Change = 190 − 160 = 30 on a base of 160 (earlier year).
% change = 30/160 × 100 = 18.75% → 18.75% increase.

questions.q: A box contains 4 red, 3 blue and 2 green tokens. Two tokens are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.x:
Ways to choose 2 red = C(4,2) = 6; ways to choose any 2 = C(9,2) = 36.
P = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 3 : 4. After 8 years, the ratio will become 23 : 28. What is P's present age?
The average age of 33 trainees in a batch is 11 years. When the instructor's age is also included, the average rises by 1 year. The instructor's age is:
questions.x:
Total of trainees = 33 × 11 = 363.
With instructor: 34 × 12 = 408.
Instructor = 408 − 363 = 45 years.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a storage tank in 10 hours and 24 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 60 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(10, 24, 60) = 120 units.
Rates: +12, +5, −2 units/hour → net 15 units/hour.
Time = 120 / 15 = 8 hours.
